kept.excerpt: La presencia de agentes estadunidenses de inteligencia en México que no informaron su estancia al gobierno federal sólo se ha detectado en Chihuahua, reiteró la presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum. Recordó que hay alrededor de 250 agentes en México, quienes cumplen con la Constitución y la ley nacional, pues han sido aprobados por un comité que revisa las solicitudes y cada mes estos agentes extranjeros de inteligencia o seguridad deben cumplir con un informe de su actuación en México.
kept.relevance: This cutoff-day report documents Mexico's position on foreign intelligence personnel and reporting requirements, without establishing direct U.S. combat participation.

kept.excerpt: Therefore, I hereby designate the aforementioned organizations and their respective aliases as Foreign Terrorist Organizations pursuant to section 219 of the INA. These designations go into effect upon publication.
kept.publisher: U.S. Department of State / Federal Register
kept.relevance: The notice designates the Juarez Cartel and Los Viagras as foreign terrorist organizations, providing recent official policy context but no evidence of a qualifying operation.

kept.excerpt: Guatemala has requested U.S. military cooperation spanning access to equipment, training, and experts to assist Guatemalan operations against drug trafficking, President Bernardo Arevalo said on Thursday. The joint plans stopped short of U.S. military operations on Guatemalan soil and fall within existing bilateral agreements, the government noted. "There is no agreement authorizing foreign military operations on national territory," the government said in a statement.
kept.relevance: Guatemala's clarification distinguishes expanded cooperation from authorization for direct U.S. military operations on its territory.

kept.excerpt: Since last year, CIA operatives inside Mexico have directly participated in deadly attacks on several, mostly mid-level cartel members, the sources said. The level of CIA involvement with operations has varied, according to the sources, from more passive intelligence sharing and providing general support to direct participation in assassination operations. After publication, CIA spokesperson Liz Lyons released a statement to CNN saying, “This is false and salacious reporting that serves as nothing more than a PR campaign for the cartels and puts American lives at risk,” without specifying what aspect of the reporting is false.
kept.relevance: This report alleges conduct relevant to the direct-participation requirement, but its anonymous sourcing and explicit CIA denial matter under the official-confirmation or overwhelming-consensus standard.

kept.excerpt: Two U.S. officials killed in a vehicle crash as they returned from destroying a clandestine drug lab in northern Mexico over the weekend were working for the CIA, according to a U.S. official and two other people familiar with the matter. The U.S. Embassy declined Monday to identify the individuals or which entity of the U.S. government they worked for, but said the officials were "supporting Chihuahua state authorities' efforts to combat cartel operations."
kept.relevance: The Chihuahua incident places U.S. personnel near an anti-cartel operation, while the embassy's support-role description leaves the qualifying nature of their participation unresolved.

kept.excerpt: On March 6, Ecuador bombed a site that officials there and in the U.S. described as a training camp for drug traffickers, using intelligence supplied by the U.S. Nearby residents later said the site was nothing more than a civilian farm. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has said more such strikes are coming as part of the new anti-cartel U.S.-Ecuador effort.
kept.relevance: This follow-up identifies both uncertainty about the Ecuador target and an intelligence-support description of the U.S. role, qualifying the initial joint-strike announcements.

kept.excerpt: In furtherance of our efforts, the Secretary of War established the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition, a pledge from military leaders and representatives from 17 countries demonstrating that the region is ready to operationalize hard power to defeat these threats to our security and civilization. The United States will train and mobilize partner nation militaries to achieve the most effective fighting force necessary to dismantle cartels and their ability to export violence and pursue influence through organized intimidation.
kept.publisher: Executive Office of the President / Federal Register
kept.relevance: The proclamation supplies official regional policy context while illustrating that training and mobilizing partners alone do not establish qualifying direct participation.

kept.excerpt: The U.S. and Ecuador carried out a joint operation targeting drug trafficking operations in the South American country, authorities in both countries said on Friday, with the U.S. calling the move “lethal kinetic operations.” The operations used helicopters, aircraft, river boats and drones to locate and bomb a drug traffickers’ training camp in north-east Ecuador near the Colombian border, Ecuador’s defense ministry said in a statement. The camp belonged to the Comandos de la Frontera (CDF), a Colombian crime group made up of FARC dissidents, and had a capacity for 50 people, it added. “At the request of Ecuador, the Department of War executed targeted action to advance our shared objective of dismantling narco-terrorist networks,” Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell wrote on X.
kept.relevance: The report records a land strike against an alleged drug-trafficking camp and an attributed Pentagon statement, making the precise U.S. operational role material to the resolution criteria.

kept.excerpt: On March 3, Ecuadorian and U.S. military forces launched operations against Designated Terrorist Organizations in Ecuador. The operations are a powerful example of the commitment of partners in Latin America and the Caribbean to combat the scourge of narco-terrorism.
kept.relevance: This primary U.S. government announcement establishes an operation in Ecuador, but its wording does not specify whether U.S. personnel directly participated in combat.

kept.excerpt: The U.S. military's role in the joint mission was the presence of military advisors in Ecuador who provided planning, intelligence, and operational support in preparation for the mission, a source familiar with the operation told ABC News. They advised Ecuadorian forces, but they did not participate in the actual ground and airlift operation, which was carried out by Ecuadorian forces, the source said.
kept.relevance: This contemporaneous clarification directly addresses the exclusion of advisory, intelligence, and support roles for the initially announced Ecuador operation.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-07-20 inclusive. The Federal Register proclamation was signed March 7 but published March 12; the July 16 designation appears on a shared Federal Register PDF page. The La Jornada excerpt is preserved in Spanish. Conflicting descriptions of U.S. participation are retained as evidence rather than treated as confirmation. Market creation date was not supplied, so earlier events are contextual evidence and are not asserted to fall within the market's qualifying window. This pack does not determine the outcome.
